analysis.investment_thesis: TENNIND is a genuinely excellent business — ROCE of 57.3% and near-zero debt signal a high-quality compounder — but the Magic Formula rejects it on valuation: Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) of ~3.6% is less than a third of the 12% minimum I require. You are paying a luxury price (P/E 42x, EV/EBITDA 26.7x) for a business exposed to an existential EV transition headwind.
key_strengths: Exceptional ROIC: ROCE of 57.3% far exceeds the 25% threshold — truly rare capital efficiency
Near debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.02) with strong FCF: INR 500 Cr in FY25, capex only 8% of EBIT
Operating margin expanded from 11.8% (FY23) to 16.7% (FY25) despite a revenue dip — pricing power at work
key_risks: Earnings Yield ~3.6% (EBIT INR 815 Cr / EV ~INR 22,900 Cr) — badly fails the 'cheap' half of the Magic Formula
Secular risk: catalytic converters, mufflers, exhaust pipes face near-certain volume decline as ICE vehicles are phased out for EVs

Cash being heavily extracted upstream: Financing CF was -INR 686 Cr (FY24) and -INR 433 Cr (FY25) — reserves fell from INR 895 Cr to INR 514 Cr in two years, likely large dividends to Mauritius parent
red_flags: Earnings Yield of ~3.6% is less than half the minimum 6% threshold — Magic Formula would not rank this stock
Revenue contracted FY25 vs FY24 (INR 4,890 Cr vs 5,468 Cr) — top-line growth is absent
Subsidiary structure with Tenneco Mauritius as promoter (74.79%) raises related-party capital extraction risk given aggressive financing outflows
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on TENNIND yields a split verdict. On Return on Capital, this is an outstanding business: ROCE of 57.3% (far above the 25% excellence threshold), capex/EBIT of just ~8%, and FCF conversion consistently above 60% of EBIT. FY25 EBIT of INR 815 Cr grew ~33% year-on-year despite a revenue decline — a sign of genuine operating leverage and pricing power. The business is essentially debt-free and has generated positive operating cash flow in all three years. On Earnings Yield, the story falls apart. Using EV/EBITDA of 26.74x and FY25 EBITDA of INR 857 Cr, implied EV ≈ INR 22,900 Cr. Earnings Yield = 815/22,900 ≈ 3.6% — less than a third of the 12% I require and below even the 6% 'not overvalued' threshold. A P/E of 42.3x on a clean-air auto parts manufacturer facing EV disruption is not a bargain.

The structural concern compounds the valuation issue. TENNIND's core products — exhaust systems, catalytic converters, mufflers — are tied entirely to internal combustion engines. The secular tailwind that drove ROCE above 50% (emissions regulations mandating aftertreatment systems) becomes a headwind as the auto fleet electrifies. Meanwhile, the Mauritius parent appears to be aggressively extracting cash: financing outflows of INR 686 Cr and INR 433 Cr in FY24/FY25 have shrunk reserves from INR 895 Cr to INR 514 Cr. For current holders, the business quality justifies a HOLD; for new buyers, the Magic Formula says wait for a far more attractive entry price.
